title: Basic Pharmacology
description: This course is an introduction to pharmacology. Topics include pharmacology terminology, drug forms, routes of administration, drug categories, and mechanisms of drug action. This course is intended for students in the Health Information Technology Program and healthcare professionals who want to refresh their working knowledge of basic pharmacology.
outcomes: Identify drug categories and list common drugs within each category.
objectives: Define basic pharmacology terms and concepts.
Compare and contrast the forms in which drugs are manufactured and align with the routes of administration.
Identify common drug categories and explain their mechanisms of action.
content: Drug categories and mechanisms of action
assignments: Textbooks and resources, including the Physician's Desk Reference (PDR).
Review of professional journals with relevant articles related to pharmacology.
Compose two 1-page typewritten summaries of professional journal articles regarding the therapeutic use of a specific new medication.
Compare two or more therapeutic strategies for disease management using different medications.
View relevant videos or television documentaries dealing with either therapeutic or illicit use of drugs.
Review professional literature for an individual or group presentation.
Interview a profession who uses pharmacology in their profession, such as a coder or pharmacist.
Given a list of medications for each of several patients, determine whether or not any one of them is contraindicated.
Determine the drug and amount found in doctor's orders.
Using case scenarios explain why a drug is being prescribed for the condition or dictation in question.
